questions.stem: A student stands $$ 4 \text{m} $$ in front of a plane mirror. How far must he/she walk in order to be $$ 2 \text{m} $$ from his/her image?
explanation_steps:

**Step 3: Calculate the walking distance.** The student started at $$ 4 \text{m} $$ and needs to reach $$ 1 \text{m} $$. 
$$ \text{Distance to walk} = 4 \text{m} - 1 \text{m} = 3 \text{m} $$

questions.stem: A stone is thrown vertically up with velocity of $$ 30 \text{ m/s} $$. At the same place after $$ 2 \text{ sec} $$ another stone is projected up with velocity of $$ 50 \text{ m/s} $$. At what time in second and at what height in meter respectively do they meet from the starting point?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Set up equations for height ($$ h $$).**
Stone 1: $$ h_1 = u_1 t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 30t - 5t^2 $$
Stone 2: $$ h_2 = u_2(t-2) - \frac{1}{2}g(t-2)^2 = 50(t-2) - 5(t-2)^2 $$

**Step 2: Set $$ h_1 = h_2 $$ to find meeting time.**
$$ 30t - 5t^2 = 50t - 100 - 5(t^2 - 4t + 4) $$
$$ 30t - 5t^2 = 50t - 100 - 5t^2 + 20t - 20 $$
$$ 30t = 70t - 120 $$
$$ 40t = 120 \Rightarrow t = 3 \text{ seconds} $$

**Step 3: Calculate height at $$ t = 3 $$.**
$$ h = 30(3) - 5(3)^2 = 90 - 45 = 45 \text{ meters} $$

Result: 3s & 45m.
